clue.text: Musical performer realistic about Shostakovich's Fifth

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters of realistic are rearranged
the fifth letter of the composer's name is taken, counting S-H-O-S-T

explanation.surface: A down-to-earth performer tackling a Shostakovich symphony, the famous Fifth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fifth' looks like the symphony, but it picks the fifth letter of Shostakovich, T. 'about' makes RECITALIS from REALISTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A recitalist gives solo recitals, so is a kind of musical performer.

clue.text: See 26
Against having label on one being kept in with disease

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: something kept in is held inside, so the letter for one goes within the label-on pair

parts.note: a tag is a label
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone labelled and kept in isolation because of an infectious illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being kept in' puts I inside TAGON, giving TAGION after CON.
explanation.definitionFit: Contagion is the spreading of illness by contact, or the illness so spread.

clue.text: Dragged along to make vows in church?

parts.note: to wed is to marry, making vows at a church service

explanation.surface: Someone hauled to the altar against their will to marry.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the wordplay is a playful split: a church wedding is not the only place vows are made.
explanation.definitionFit: A towed vehicle is pulled along behind another by a rope or bar.

clue.text: European region left with a scheme outdated ultimately

parts.note: a plan is a scheme

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of outdated is taken

explanation.surface: A region abandoned along with a scheme that eventually became obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapland is the far-northern area spanning Norway, Sweden, Finland and Russia.

clue.text: Holy person has posh car? Walks!

parts.note: ST abbreviates saint, a holy person
a Rolls, short for Rolls-Royce, is a luxury car

explanation.surface: Surprise that a saint owns a luxury car, with the retort that he walks.
explanation.definitionFit: Strolls are leisurely walks, used here as a plural noun or verb.

clue.text: Very impressive record — I start to cheer

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here of cheer

explanation.surface: An outstanding record makes the speaker begin to cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic as an adjective means grand or heroic in scale, hence very impressive.

clue.text: Military chaplain has living accommodation with soldiers

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or home
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: An army chaplain living in quarters alongside the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is the forces' name for a chaplain, from the Spanish and Italian for father.

clue.text: Fair game in which hitter looks for success

definitions.text: Fair game in which hitter looks for success

parts.words: Fair game in which hitter looks for success
parts.note: a stall at a funfair where a player throws balls hoping to knock a nut off its stand

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a batter in a sport chasing a good result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair game' means a game at a fair, a British funfair stall; the 'hitter' is the thrower aiming to dislodge the target, and 'shy' means a throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground stall where balls are thrown at coconuts balanced on posts, the prize being any knocked off.

clue.text: Second criminal about 50 is illicit dealer

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the criminal goes round the fifty

parts.note: a mugger is a street robber, a criminal
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A second offender, roughly fifty years old, trading in illegal goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A smuggler moves goods illegally across borders, a dealer in contraband.

clue.text: We turned against wickedness, showing physical strength

parts.note: sin is wickedness

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the word we is read backwards

explanation.surface: People taking a stand against evil and proving their muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew is tendon, and by extension muscular power or strength.

clue.text: Admire a PC, exceptional person rendering emergency help

indicators.note: exceptional suggests out of the ordinary, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Praise for a police constable who is an outstanding first responder.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramedic is a trained medical worker who treats people at the scene before hospital.

clue.text: No-nonsense approach of a rural dean confronting bishop in room

indicators.note: in places the clergy inside the room

parts.note: a hall is a room

indicators.note: confronting means facing, so the dean comes up against the bishop, next to it

parts.note: RD abbreviates rural dean, a Church of England office
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A tough stance taken by a church dean facing down his bishop in a meeting room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ARDB inside HALL, splitting it as H-ARDB-ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing hardball means using tough, uncompromising tactics.

clue.text: Never good backing a politician with specialist agenda?

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: ne'er is a poetic contraction of never

explanation.surface: Never a good idea to support a single-issue politician.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: a Green's agenda is environmental.
explanation.definitionFit: A Green is a member of an environmentalist party, whose focus is ecology.

clue.text: A demon a bit naughty is loathed

indicators.note: naughty implies misbehaving, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A slightly mischievous demon is hated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' links the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To abominate is to detest utterly, so abominated means loathed.

clue.text: Brusque editor's given the necessary information

parts.note: brief can mean curt or brusque

explanation.surface: A curt editor has passed on the essential facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 's stands for has, joining the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be briefed is to have been informed and instructed before a task.

clue.text: Resolution of company head

parts.note: a firm is a company
a ness is a headland, a head projecting into the sea

explanation.surface: A decision taken by a company's boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' reads as a boss but means a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolution in the sense of determination is firmness of purpose.

clue.text: Court finally finds nothing within the law

indicators.note: finally means the last letter, here of finds

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing
licit means permitted by law, so within the law

explanation.surface: A judge's tribunal concludes that nothing is outside legal bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a law court but is the verb to court, to seek favour. 'within' links nothing to the law.
explanation.definitionFit: To solicit is to seek or woo, as to court someone's support.

clue.text: Lots of countries showing self-restraint

definitions.meaning: a large landmass holding many countries
... as an adjective means exercising self-control

explanation.surface: Many nations demonstrating restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Continent names both a great landmass and, as an adjective, the virtue of self-control.

clue.text: Fellow more confident after losing face as muck-spreader

indicators.note: after puts the trimmed word behind the fellow

parts.note: a man is a fellow

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: surer means more confident

explanation.surface: A man grows more self-assured after a humiliation, becoming a farm worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing face' takes S off SURER, leaving URER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who manures fields spreads muck on them as fertiliser.

clue.text: Being let out again brings liberation

definitions.meaning: a ... is a renewed letting of property

explanation.surface: Getting out a second time brings freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the word as RE-LEASE, a property being leased again.
explanation.definitionFit: Release is the act of setting free, and re-lease is letting a property once more.

clue.text: My home — this is being demolished in old city

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like my!
in means at home

indicators.note: demolished means knocked down, so the word is is removed from this

explanation.surface: An exclamation as someone's house is torn down in an ancient town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is the exclamation COR, not a possessive. 'being demolished' strips IS from THIS, leaving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Corinth was an ancient Greek city-state on the isthmus joining the Peloponnese to the mainland.

clue.text: Hide in study — set apart, by the sound of it

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: the second piece is spoken, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: to seal off is to close something off and keep it apart

explanation.surface: Taking refuge in a study, apparently cut off from others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' is the verb. 'in' links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal is to keep out of sight, to hide.

clue.text: President giving refusal in Paris, one cross inside

indicators.note: inside places the one and cross within the French refusal

parts.note: non is French for no
I is the Roman numeral one
X is a cross

explanation.surface: A president turning something down in Paris, with one person angry inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' reads as angry but is the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Nixon was the 37th President of the United States.

clue.text: Kiss given to no one turning up — I'm inert!

parts.note: X is a kiss at the end of a letter

indicators.note: in a down answer turning up reverses the word, read from bottom to top

parts.note: none means no one

explanation.surface: Someone kisses, nobody responds, and they declare themselves lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenon is a noble gas, one of the chemically inert elements, speaking in the first person.

clue.text: Light lager knocked back with 'rocky' movement?

parts.note: to light on is to land, as a bird alights

indicators.note: knocked back means read backwards here, not drunk down

parts.note: pils is a pilsner lager

explanation.surface: A light lager downed, and a drinker moves unsteadily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' suggests drinking but reverses PILS. 'Light' is the verb meaning to come down.
explanation.definitionFit: A landslip is a fall of earth and rock down a slope, a movement of rocks.

clue.text: Salvationists beat the devil

parts.note: SA is the Salvation Army, whose members are Salvationists
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: Salvation Army members defeating the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Satan is the name of the Devil in Christian tradition.

clue.text: Highly ranked US statesman once

parts.note: a former US Secretary of State whose first name is also a senior church rank

explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly ranked' hints at the first name, a dean being a senior clergyman or college official.
explanation.definitionFit: He served as Secretary of State under Presidents Kennedy and Johnson in the 1960s.

clue.text: Salt given report of taster, say

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the first word is spoken aloud

parts.note: the tongue is the organ that tastes
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A salt given a taster's verdict, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: A tungstate is a salt of tungstic acid, a chemical compound.

clue.text: The first person to offer a unifying idea

parts.note: me is a first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: The leader stepping forward with a concept that ties everything together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first person' reads as a pioneer but is the grammatical first person. 'to offer' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the central subject or motif that runs through a work.

clue.text: Academic, good and sound

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A lecturer who is both decent and reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable but is the noun, a bell's ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Dong is the deep ringing noise of a large bell.

clue.text: PM to get the boot!

definitions.meaning: the Duke of ... was a British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: Calls for a Prime Minister to be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get the boot' means be fired, but here 'the boot' names the rubber boot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke of Wellington was Prime Minister, and the waterproof wellington boot is named after him.
